steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Boolean logic is a form of algebra where all values are either TRUE (1) or FALSE (0). It is named after mathematician George Boole and forms the basis of how computers make decisions.

steps.title: NOT gate
steps.body: Takes a single input and produces the opposite (inverted) output. If input is 1, output is 0. If input is 0, output is 1. Also called an inverter.

steps.title: AND gate
steps.body: Takes two inputs and outputs 1 (TRUE) only if BOTH inputs are 1. If either or both inputs are 0, the output is 0.

steps.title: OR gate
steps.body: Takes two inputs and outputs 1 (TRUE) if EITHER or BOTH inputs are 1. The output is 0 only when both inputs are 0.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Draw the truth table for Q = A . B | A circuit has the expression Q = (A OR B) AND NOT C. Draw the full truth table. | What is the difference between OR and XOR? Give a real-world example of each.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Q = A . NOT B: A=0 B=0 Q=0; A=0 B=1 Q=0; A=1 B=0 Q=1; A=1 B=1 Q=0. Output is 1 only when A=1 AND B=0. | Three inputs = 8 rows. Q=1 only when (A=1 OR B=1) AND C=0. Rows where Q=1: (0,1,0), (1,0,0), (1,1,0). All other rows Q=0. | OR outputs 1 if either or both inputs are 1. XOR outputs 1 only if the inputs are different. OR example: alarm if front OR back door is open. XOR example: staircase light controlled by two switches -

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always show intermediate columns in truth tables - marks are awarded for working Learn the Boolean notation: dot = AND, plus = OR, overbar = NOT When drawing circuits from expressions, work from the inside out (brackets first) For 3-input truth tables, count in binary: 000, 001, 010, 011, 100, 101, 110, 111 Remember order of operations: NOT, then AND, then OR Practise converting between expressions, circuits, and truth tables in both directions
